nodes.label: Chrono_core Library Target
nodes.rationale: Single target aggregating core, serialization, physics, contact, links, collision, Bullet, multicore-collision and third-party sources; exposed to consumers as the Chrono::core alias with Eigen3::Eigen as a PUBLIC dependency and the bullet and HACDv2 directories on the public include path.

nodes.label: ChCorePCH.h Precompiled Header
nodes.rationale: Chrono_core has ~500 translation units almost all of which include the core linear-algebra headers plus STL streams/containers; Build-Insights profiling showed these dominate front-end parse and template-instantiation cost, with Eigen topping instantiations and ChMatrix.h the single most-included header. ChMatrix.h is the deliberate anchor rather than a bare Eigen include because it defines EIGEN_MATRIXBASE_PLUGIN / EIGEN_SPARSEMATRIX_PLUGIN before pulling in Eigen/Dense and Eigen/Sparse, reproducing Chrono's exact Eigen configuration and transitively precompiling ChArchive.h and ChArchiveASCII.h. Scope is PRIVATE so consumers are not forced onto the PCH, and the header is guarded by __cplusplus so it is empty for C sources.

nodes.label: Embedded Bullet Collision Source Group
nodes.rationale: The cbt-prefixed Bullet sources are compiled directly into Chrono_core (via ChCollisionSystemBullet / ChCollisionModelBullet wrappers) rather than linked as an external Bullet library.

nodes.label: Multicore Collision Detection Source Group
nodes.rationale: ChCollisionSystemMulticore, broadphase, narrowphase (MPR and PRIMS) and ray test sources are added to Chrono_core only when CHRONO_THRUST_FOUND; otherwise the file lists are emptied so the same target definition still configures.

nodes.label: External Code Warning Suppression
nodes.rationale: Bullet, HACDv2, V-HACD and tiny_obj sources get per-source COMPILE_OPTIONS (-Wno-everything / /w / -w) so third-party code cannot drown out warnings from Chrono's own sources while the project still builds at -Wall or /W4.

nodes.label: Bullet Compile Definitions
nodes.rationale: BT_THREADSAFE and BP_USE_FIXEDPOINT_INT_32 are always set; BT_USE_DOUBLE_PRECISION and BT_USE_OPENMP are driven by the CH_USE_BULLET_DOUBLE and CH_USE_BULLET_OPENMP options, the latter dependent on CH_ENABLE_OPENMP.

nodes.label: FEA and FEA-MULTIPHYSICS Options
nodes.rationale: FEA is part of the core library rather than a separate module directory; FEA-MULTIPHYSICS is a cmake_dependent_option that can only be on when FEA is on.
